newsitem.title: UK: Only U.S. planes involved in Iraq attack - Britain.
newsitem.headline: Only U.S. planes involved in Iraq attack - Britain.

text.p: The Western allies are extending the no-fly zone over southern Iraq in response to President Saddam Hussein's build-up of forces and the attack on a key Kurdish city, Britain said on Tuesday.

"The no-fly zone in southern Iraq will be extended to allow the allies operating there to have a greater opportunity to control more of Saddam's airspace and bring greater control over him," Defence Secretary Michael Portillo told BBC radio.
Speaking as U.S. warplanes pounded Iraqi air defence targets, Portillo said that British aircraft had not taken part in the operation.
"My understanding is that this is a purely Cruise missile attack and therefore only United States air forces are involved," he told BBC radio in an interview.
"This operation did not involve British attack aircraft. We were asked and granted logistics support to the Americans," Portillo added.

"The Americans have launched a number of military attacks against rural areas. They are purely military targets. They have been selected to minimise collateral damage, that is to say loss of civilian life," Portillo said. He gave no further details.

Britain said Saddam had been informed earlier on Tuesday that the no-fly zone in southern Iraq was being extended in response to his recent force build-up and last weekend's attack on the Kurdish city of Arbil.

British officials indicated that the extension of the no-fly zone was intended to be a permanent arrangement. United Nations approval was not expected to be sought since the "safe haven" was set up by the international community. It is patrolled by British, French and U.S. planes.

A statement from Prime Minister John Major's office said Britain fully supported the U.S. attack, describing it as an "unequivocal message to Saddam Hussein that repression of innocent civilians and reckless acts of brutality are unacceptable."
"We would like to see the broadest support from the international community for what has been done," Portillo said.
"Much of the international community, even if they have difficulties in expressing this, will understand that Saddam Hussein is an appalling dictator." he added.
